p:cNvPr.descr: The pyrimidines cytosine, thymine (DNA), and uracil (RNA). Cytosine is a single 6-sided ring structure. The apical C bonds up to NH2, double bonds down and left to N, which bonds down to C. C double bonds down and left to O and down and right to NH. NH bonds up and right to CH, which double bonds up to CH, which bonds up and left to the initial C. To the right is thymine (DNA). It is similar to the structure of cysotine, but its apical C double bonds up to O and down and left to NH, and its final C bonds up and right to CH3. To the right is uracil (RNA). The structure is identical to that of thymine, but it is missing the CH3 bonded to the final C.
